The defining factors are:  high maneuverability with a large control range and maintaining the efficiency of the equipment in the control range while reducing power to a technical minimum.
For the Facility, due to the significant influence of  the outside air temperature on the GT power, the nominal and maximum power values and the limits of the control range change significantly with the change in the outside air temperature.
The indicators of installed capacity and maneuverability for each type of power equipment are determined in the Project by the technical characteristics of the equipment and are specified during the annual certification of power units.
The installed electrical power of condensing combined cycle plants is determined as the sum of the  capacities  of steam  and  gas  turbines  at  an  average  annual  temperature,  air  humidity  and  the corresponding temperature of the cooling water.
The determination of the average annual generation of electrical energy was made on the basis of  simulated graphs of  the dependence of  electrical power on the ambient temperature (Figure 1.3.1). In doing so, it is accepted:

- «base» mode of operation is taken below the technical minimum;
- within the regulation range, the coefficient of influence of the participation of equipment in the regulation of  daily schedules of  electrical loads (0.5) was applied to the volume of  electricity generation.

The main fuel that provides production activities for the generation of  electricity of  the designed Facility, is fuel (natural and associated) gas provided by «QazaqGaz» JSC from two sources:
- Main gas pipeline (MGP) «Beineu-Bozoi-Shymkent» (main);
- -Main gas pipeline (MGP) «BGR-TBA» (reserve).
To provide the projected power plant with fuel gas, the construction of the linear part of  the gas pipeline-outlet with AGDS was considered, which ensures the transportation and supply of natural gas with the declared volume of consumption.
The equipment of  the external gas supply system includes the following units:
- security crane units (SCU);
- cleaning device launch unit (CDLU), cleaning device receiving unit (CDRU);
- automated gas distribution station (AGDS);
- gas pipeline.
Power supply of  the site AGDS - «CCGT», CDRU, CDLU, SCU is carried out from the projected OTLPW-10 kV (overhead transmission lines with protected wires) for auxiliary needs of the CCGT.
Steel  pipes  of the  gas  pipeline  provide  for  measures  to  protect  engineering  networks  from corrosion.  The  external  gas supply  complex  is provided with  communication  and signaling  systems: fiber optic communication, industrial and technological USW  (ultra-short waves) radio communication, satellite communication, IP telephony, burglar alarm, fire alarm, video surveillance.
The complex of  all measures to ensure the reliable operation of  all units of  the gas supply system makes it possible to ensure uninterrupted supply of  fuel gas from the main gas pipeline to the site of  the designed combined-cycle plant with the required parameters.
fOCT 305-82 (GOST 305-82) diesel fuel is provided as an emergency fuel for gas turbines.
For the storage of a 3 -day supply of fuel, a diesel fuel warehouse is provided, the total capacity is determined by the project. A diesel fuel pumping station is provided for receiving and pumping diesel fuel.
To replenish the emergency reserve of  diesel fuel, it is transported by road and/or rail to the sites.

In order to ensure  the specified  control  range,  the average hourly  power of a  CCGT  with a maneuverable generation mode is allowed no more than 0.5 of the control power.
The technical minimum also includes an environmental minimum that meets the requirements for NOx emissions at the lowest possible power.
The use of  the CCGT control range, taking into account the technical minimum, allows the use of  industrial gas turbines, instead of  aircraft derivatives, the use of  a standard maintenance schedule and repair periods without increasing the equivalent operating hours with frequent starts. The assessment of the  cost of  the entire life  cycle of  a maneuverable power plant includes both capital costs and service costs, taking into account the requirements for the number of  starts.
For the industrial gas turbines under consideration, the requirement of  at least 350 starts/year can only be achieved by significantly reducing the overhaul period and the service life of  the plants, which is inappropriate. The optimal solution for the tasks of the widest regulation is the aircraft-derived GT, operating in a simple cycle, if  necessary.
Industrial grade GT have different wear rates in base mode and in cyclic mode.
Thermal mechanical fatigue is the life limiting factor for peak duty units, while creep, oxidation and corrosion are life limiting factors for base duty units.
The maintenance interval is determined by which criterion limit is reached first.
The  normal  start-up  cycle  of a  CCGT  unit  from  a  cold  state  to  a  full  load  of 100%  1s approximately 4 hours.
The normal start-up cycle of  a CCGT unit from a hot state, in which less than 8 hours have passed from the moment of  shutdown to the moment of  start-up, until reaching 100% load, is approximately 2.5 hours. At the same time, a set of  approximately 80% of  the power takes about 30-40 minutes. With the use of modem methods, this time can be significantly reduced. The more powerful the equipment, the longer it will start.
Fast start in a simple cycle from any state applies only to aircraft-derived GT and some industrial GT up to 100 MW. It is these GT in a simple cycle that are most often used in world practice to solve the problems of  ensuring network flexibility and emergency backup of  renewable energy sources.

The HRSG is a drum boiler with natural circulation in high and low pressure evaporative circuits, single-shell, horizontal profile,  suspended from its own frame through intermediate metal structures, with a deaerator built into the LP drum. The framework is executed on high-strength bolts.
To ensure the operation of the GT in open cycle mode (when the HRSG is off), the HRSG is equipped with a bypass system including:
- bypass valve (divertor);
- shut-off  valve guillotine type;
- -a  bypass  chimney  with  stairs,  platforms,  built-in  silencer,  light  protection  and  lightning protection.
The HRSG is designed to operate on combustion products coming from the GT. The main and reserve fuel for GT is dry natural gas. Emergency fuel - diesel.
The main HRSG equipment is installed in the building.
For  access  and  ease  of maintenance  of equipment  and  fittings,  stairs  and  platforms  with galvanized flooring are provided.
The maximum gas temperature at the inlet to the HRSG is 580 °C (to be specified after receiving data on the GT).
The HRSG and flues are made gas-tight, based on the excess gas pressure of 3.5 kPa. The way to ensure gas tightness is sheathing and sealing.
The heating surfaces of the HRSG are made of  pipes with external slotted and continuous spiral­ band finning. The location of  the heat exchange pipes of  the heating surfaces is vertical.
The HRSG design provides complete drainage of heating surfaces and pipelines, as well as the possibility of  pre-start, operational, chemical and water flushing, conservation.
The HRSG layout provides for places for tracing cable routes, impulse pipes, and also provides the ability to install the necessary measuring devices, fittings, fittings, bosses and other selected devices for CMI, automation and protection in places convenient for maintenance.
The wall material of  the high-pressure drum is selected from the condition of  the minimum startup time of  the HRSG from a cold state.
The HRSG has manual devices for sampling water and steam, made of  stainless steel.
The HRSG design provides for the possibility of  maintaining it in a hot standby.
The HRSG is supplied in blocks. The design of  the HRSG provides installation both with supply blocks and with mounting blocks with their enlargement at the construction site.
The design of the HRSG and the delivery  blockiness of its units  was  developed taking into account the technology of  manufacturing, transportation, installation, repair and operation.
The supply of  HRSG is carried out in prefabricated blocks of maximum overall dimensions and maximum factory completeness of parts, based on the conditions of loading and unloading operations, transportation and storage. Coefficient of delivery blockiness is not less than 80% of  the calculated mass ofHRSG.

Fixed-position cameras with fixed focal length lenses and pan-tilt zoom (PTZ) cameras should be used to provide  adequate coverage.  Remote control of PTZ  cameras should be provided.  Camera systems must be digital systems that must be user-configurable, scale, use digital storage devices, and be distributed over large networks.

The  function  «Registration  of  emergency  situations»  (RES)  should  be  provided  for  the accumulation  and  presentation  on  screens  and  (or)  printing  of data  on  the  process  of occurrence, development  and  elimination  of emergency  situations  with  reference  to  astronomical  time  with  an accuracy of 1  ms. The RES function should ensure the registration of, as a rule, reliable technological data for  the period preceding  the  accident  and after its  occurrence,  on the operation of the main and auxiliary equipment, the operation of protections, interlocks, automatic control devices and personnel.
All information involved in the RES is conditionally divided into three groups:
- A - analog and discrete signals characterizing the state of control objects, the registration cycle of  which corresponds to the cycle of  updating information on monitor screens;
- B - analog and discrete signals characterizing the state of  control objects that require registration with high resolution;
- C - initiative signals for the operation of electrical and technological protections, event signals associated  with  the  impact  of personnel on control  objects,  which are  also  subject to the  actions  of technological and electrical protections, event signals associated with the output of analog parameters beyond  the  alarm settings  or  operation of protections,  and also  the  values  of analog  parameters  for electrical equipment that require registration with super high resolution.
It is necessary to have recorders of  different time characteristics for: - thermal power equipment; -electrical equipment; - electrical equipment associated with the receipt of  signals from AEA.
It is advisable to have several (the number corresponds to the purpose of  the project) independent registrars of emergency situations (ES) in the HSC for units and assemblies.  The recorders can work simultaneously and independently and  record  arbitrary  sets  of parameters  spe�ified  at  the  stages  of development and operation of the system.
The following enlarged RES algorithm should be provided. Prior to the arrival of a signal about the  beginning  of an  emergency,  there  should  be  a  constant  sliding  accumulation of data in  the  pre­ emergency interval. When an initiating signal characterizing an accident appears, all the accumulated data are «frozen» and the process of registering the development and localization of the accident in the post-accident interval begins.
The RES function should not take into account the real states of  the protections (  enabled, enabled in the information mode - signaled). Recorders in the mode of  post-emergency recording of information should not be switched if the triggered protection is signaled.
The imitation of the beginning of the ES is provided to check the functionality of the function when testing the equipment.
Information about the accident is recorded in the archive.

Changes in the technological protection settings are made by service personnel with access authorization, recorded in the archive and accompanied by mandatory logging.

It is necessary to provide that all mechanical, electrical and control equipment of the power plant, etc. provide free access for periodic maintenance throughout the life of the power plant.

- One worker in conditions of free access can lift a weight of  no more than 30 kg.
- Two workers, each with free access, can lift a total of about 45 kg.

If  it is planned to use an overhead crane for maintenance, this must be specifically provided for in the plan for the use of  cranes, indicating the location of  the cranes and equipment, indicating the load capacity of the equipment. The use of tooling with obviously higher load capacity for light parts should be avoided due to the difficulty of  access.
The clearance to the front work surface at the point of service must be at least 600 mm and preferably greater than 750 mm. All  buildings  and  structures  must  have  complete  automated  heating,  ventilation  and  air conditioning (HV  AC) systems, consisting of  the necessary air conditioning units, fans, heaters, control units and other things.

The HV  AC systems should be designed to shut down in the event of a fire alarm, pressurize supply and exhaust ducts as required for clean agent fire extinguishing systems, and start pressurization systems. When planning and conducting tests for compliance with guaranteed indicators, the Contractor shall comply with the requirements described in the form «Guaranteed indicators».
The  Contractor  allocates  for  planning  and  conducting  tests  for  compliance  with  guaranteed indicators, as well as for the preparation of reports on them by an independent, well-reviewed, qualified company (the «Testing company»). The choice and appointment of the Testing company is approved by the Customer.
During the tests, the power plant is operated by the Customer's personnel under the supervision of  the Contractor.
The  Contractor  describes  the  methodology  for  measuring  the  required  parameters,  and  also provides information on the expected standards and accuracy of  instrumentation, expected measurement points and attaches the necessary documentation.
For each case of  failure to achieve the guaranteed performance due to the fault of  the Contractor (manufacturer of goods), the Contractor shall pay a penalty in the amount specified in the Contract.
The output electrical power is measured in the high voltage cell of the switchgear.
Current and voltage transformers are supplied by the Contractor to measure useful output power, generator power and auxiliary power. They must generally comply with the requirements for equipment, except that the current transformers must have an accuracy class of 0.1, and voltage transformers must have  an  accuracy class of 0.2  according to  IEC  60044-1  and  IEC  60044-2.  The Contractor submits calibration documents for all transformers.
Power kilowatt-hour meters for own needs for efficiency and performance testing are provided by the  Contractor. These  meters  shall  comply  with  accuracy class  0.5  according to  IEC  60521  and accuracy class 0.5 according to IEC 60687. The current and voltage transformers associated with these kilowatt-hour meters are also supplied by the Contractor and comply with the standards specified in the Contract.
On HRSGs, tests are carried out for the purity of steam (water) on them. Tests are carried out at all loads using permanently installed high-speed samplers. Particular attention is paid to situations with a change in load or unstable conditions, when mechanical transfer is most likely.
A sample of the fuel used in the tests is taken at the beginning, during and at the end of  the tests for compliance with the guaranteed performance. The necessary equipment for taking and storing fuel samples is  supplied by the  Contractor. During each sampling period,  three separate  samples will be taken,  i.e. a  total of nine  samples will be taken.  One  sample  from  each set  of three  samples is  fully analyzed by an independent body, the costs of  such analyzes are borne by the Contractor. Hierarchical structure of  works (hereinafter referred to as the HSW) provides a logical framework for project management planning, reporting and control, and has been prepared to describe the Program with an increasing level of detail for adequate management visibility. The HSW covers all phases of  the project and provides a consistent coding structure throughout, accommodating the various requirements of all parts of  the Program.
The HSW reflects the set of works to be performed by the Contractor and all third parties that may be involved in the Program. The HSW will be a common identifier between time/cost/documents and will be used to ensure integration of  time, cost, document and program resource elements.
The Contractor will install a HSW that will allow structuring information about the project at different levels of detail for different organizations. The HSW will include an alphanumeric numbering system that uniquely identifies each element of the HSW, ensuring transparency in both directions (top to bottom and bottom to top). The Contractor shall submit the Hierarchical structure of works (HSW) to the Customer for approval.
The  Contractor  will be responsible for  including  the  appropriate  WDS  number in the master schedule, organizing and grouping works according to the approved structure. The Contracting Surveyor will  include  the  same structure  in  the  Cost  Coding  System to  accurately  reflect  all  associated  costs budgeted, accepted and expended. In this way, he can develop cost reports related to budget/cost incurred at each level of the HSW structure, which will now be converted to a cost breakdown structure (CBS). The Contractor warrants that:
- The HSW includes all the tasks that must be completed during the implementation phases of  the project. The HSW is developed using the software application and hosted on a server.
- The HSW identifier (alphanumeric) is included in the cost breakdown structure to provide integration between time, cost, and documents.
- The  HSW  identifier  (alphanumeric)  is  entered  into  all  documents  to  identify  all documents and allow integration with the above parameters (cost, schedule, and documents).
The advantage of  having all three control components linked together via a WDS number allows close monitoring of project progress at all times, and easy access and monitoring of emerging issues.

The  manufacturer's  test  equipment  must  be  of  satisfactory  quality  and  condition  and,  if necessary, must be properly calibrated  in  accordance  with  international  standards  by an  accredited laboratory at the expense of  the Contractor.
After the conclusion of the Contract and clarification of the main features of the project, the Contractor will develop a detailed Manufacturer's Inspection and Test Plan, as described earlier in this document, for each item of  equipment.
The Contractor shall notify the Customer at least forty-five (  45) working days prior to any such testing. The tests must be witnessed and verified by the Customer. All activities for visiting the plant and acceptance tests (travel, reception and hotel accommodation) for the Customer will be organized at his expense at the request of the Customer.
After the inspection, carried out in front of  witnesses at the manufacturing plant, all parties must sign  the  protocol  (inspection  report)  indicating  the  subject,  participants,  results  and  comments  and distribute it immediately after the test. A detailed test report with certified copies of all tests, data and results themselves shall be distributed by the Contractor to the Customer.
Under no circumstances should equipment be shipped, or even packaged, prepared for shipment, or dismantled for the purpose of packaging for shipment, unless it has been satisfactorily inspected and approved for shipment, or inspection has been denied in writing.
The  following  equipment  must  be  subjected  to  a  Factory  Acceptance  Test  (FAT)  to prove  that reliability,  operation  and  performance  meet  the  requirements  of certain  specifications  and  relevant standards:
- Gas turbine (GT)
- Steam turbine (ST)
- HRSG
- Generators

- Lifting mechanism (bridge cranes).
All other factory equipments requested by the Customer.

The Contractor is responsible for preparing Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) for all works at the Site  and  for  each  equipment  and  submitting  them  to  the  Customer  for  review  and  approval.  The Contractor shall ensure that ITP determines critical  manufacturing steps, acceptance  criteria (  codes, standards,  drawings,  etc.)  and  specific  methods  and  procedures  to  be  used  to  meet  all  project requirements.
The ITP may take any form consistent with the Contractor's system, but must, as a minimum:
- a) Critical stages of  construction/installation and every point of  inspection and testing.
- b) Characteristics to be checked, examined and tested at each point, as well as reference drawings, procedures and acceptance criteria used.
- c) Test frequency criteria.
- d) Quality «checkpoints» (H, W, R) set by the supplier and Contractor,  which  require the verification of  selected characteristics of a document, product or process before that work can proceed. The Customer may assign additional Quality Control Points (H, W, R) to the Contractor on a case-by­ case basis.
- e) Supporting document for use (manufacturer's instructions, material certificates, laboratory test results, etc.) .
The  Contractor  shall  also  submit  copies  of  the  reference  documents/standards/acceptance codes/testing and inspection procedures, etc. referred to in the ITP along with the ITP.
All ITPs will be presented to the Customer 14 days prior to the commencement of field work. Inspection tests will be carried out after mutual agreement between the Customer and the Contractor.

Off-site  inspections  are  inspections  of  the  facilities  and/or  products  of  manufacturers  and suppliers off-site, if considered necessary and/or required by the Contract specifications, to ensure that all  requirements  are  met  and  observed.  Off-site  inspections  will  be  carried out  by  the  Customer as required. The Customer's personnel must, at any reasonable time:
- a) have full access to all parts of  the Site and to all places where inert materials come from;
- b) during production, manufacture and construction (  on the Site and elsewhere) have the right to inspect, inspect, measure and test the materials and workmanship, as well as to check the progress of  the Plant and the production and manufacture of the Materials.
A  visit  to  the  manufacturer's  plant  (travel,  reception  and  hotel)  will  be  organized  by  the Contractor at its own expense at the request of  the Customer.
The results of  each inspection will be documented in an offsite inspection report. The Contractor must  be  notified  of any  deficiencies  and must  submit  a  corrective  action  report.  All  materials  and equipment inspected off  site will be properly stored and permanently labeled with the project name and other relevant data to ensure long-term follow-up.
Materials inspections are conducted upon receipt of product delivery of  any given facility. The Customer will inspect and supervise the Contractor's physical inspection of  the materials to ensure that they have been properly stored and conform to the approved shop drawings and/or submitted product data. This will be documented in the Contractor's daily reports and the relevant project log by using a material receipt record. Equipment or materials that do not pass inspection upon receipt should not be released to production, and rejected items should be separated and included in the non-conformity report.

The Customer shall develop a procedure that defines the methodology and the associated roles and responsibilities for the control of  nonconformities related to the product and the quality process. The procedure should include a format for documenting nonconformities (Nonconformity Report Form). The Contractor will be required to implement this procedure.
If defects in material,  work  performed or  installation  are found, the Customer will notify the Contractor by issuing a Non-Conformity Report (NCR). Upon receipt of such notice, the Contractor shall immediately take steps to prevent the inadvertent use or supply of  certain nonconforming material, work or installation.
Upon receipt of the NCR, the Contractor shall immediately investigate the matter and prepare corrective actions in relation to measures to eliminate the identified non-conformities and submit them to the Customer for review and approval.
If the Customer approves the proposed corrective actions, the Contractor shall implement the proposed measures and upon completion resubmit the NCR to the Customer for closure.
The Contractor and suppliers effectively apply documented procedures that ensure that any non­ conforming product is prevented from unintended use or installation.
The  Contractor  shall  maintain  a  Register  of Nonconformities  to  indicate  the  status  of  all nonconformities that have been identified by the Customer and the Contractor. The Customer reserves the right to inspect and audit these documents at any time.

The Customer can conduct scheduled and unscheduled inspections and quality audits. When conducting scheduled audits, the Contractor will be notified of the quality audit at least five (05) days in advance.
